findings.body:
**Keep all finding fields in the deferred-debt projection.**

The blocked-cycle projection (Lines 464-468) and the terminal projection (Lines 383-387) now keep `line`, `rule`, `evidence`, and `evidenceV1`. This deferred-debt projection drops them. The persisted record therefore loses anchoring data on the debt path only. `sameFindingContent` compares these fields, so any later disposition match against these rows also fails closed.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
                     text: finding.excerpt ?? '',
                     ...(finding.fileName !== undefined ? { file: finding.fileName } : {}),
+                    ...(finding.line !== undefined ? { line: finding.line } : {}),
+                    ...(finding.rule !== undefined ? { rule: finding.rule } : {}),
+                    ...(finding.evidence !== undefined ? { evidence: finding.evidence } : {}),
+                    ...(finding.evidenceV1 !== undefined ? { evidenceV1: finding.evidenceV1 } : {}),
                     status: disposition?.action ?? 'open',
```
</details>
findings.title: Keep all finding fields in the deferred-debt projection.

findings.body:
**Guard the final `readCurrentEnrollment` call. The op must return a result, not throw.**

`readCurrentEnrollment` throws when the predecessor lineage is missing, conflicts, or cycles (`src/ops/dev/internal/deferredLedger.ts:303-306`). The call at `src/ops/review/run.ts:1104-1108` has no `try`. It also runs on every successful run, including runs with no deferred debt. If one retained `vendor-debt` lineage is inconsistent, `review.run` rejects after the findings record is persisted. The caller then gets an exception instead of `needs-human`. The refresh path at Line 995 handles the same call inside a `try`.

Map the throw to `needs-human` with `report: record`.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-      const ancestry = readCurrentEnrollment(
-        effects.openLedger(state.branch).load(),
-        currentIdentity,
-        target,
-      );
+      let ancestry: ReturnType<typeof readCurrentEnrollment>;
+      try {
+        ancestry = readCurrentEnrollment(
+          effects.openLedger(state.branch).load(),
+          currentIdentity,
+          target,
+        );
+      } catch (error) {
+        return {
+          status: 'needs-human',
+          reason: `review.run: authorized enrollment lineage could not be read — ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}`,
+          report: record,
+        };
+      }
```
</details>

As per path instructions: "a public op maps failure onto the frozen taxonomy (status 'failed' with error), never a fabricated ok."
findings.title: Guard the final `readCurrentEnrollment` call. The op must return a result, not throw.

findings.body:
**Wrap the evidence-preparation reads. Unguarded rejections escape `review.run`.**

Every other `runCommand` and `readWorktreeFile` call in this function is wrapped and mapped to `failed` (Lines 497-510, 537-550, 562-569). The new reads at Line 624 (`git show`) and Line 637 (`readWorktreeFile`) are not wrapped. `runCommand` rejects on spawn faults and on `maxBuffer` overflow (`src/ops/dev/effects.ts:207-227`). A large tracked file in the diff can trigger the overflow. With `prepareEvidence: true`, that rejection escapes `execute` after the scan and the drift check. The wrapper at Line 1168 then rethrows it.

Wrap the loop body in one `try` and return `{ status: 'failed', error: 'review.run: could not prepare evidence for ...' }`. Another option is to record the missing blob as `undefined`.

As per path instructions: "a public op maps failure onto the frozen taxonomy ... never a fabricated ok."
findings.title: Wrap the evidence-preparation reads. Unguarded rejections escape `review.run`.
